I guess it comes down to if Windows can see what I have on my Linux partition (I think it cant since its ext4).

I would love to switch to Linux full time, but need windows occasionally for work when im at home. Im going to dual boot, and try to use windows as little as I possibly can. Im a little nervous of the possibility of windows being able to read my linux partition and see whats on there, or even worse - somehow "infect" my linux install.

Hopefully its nothing to worry about. but I was just wondering if anyone here knew for sure.
Anyway having windows 10 installed on a separate partition could compromise Linux?

You answered your own question.
Windows can not see an ext4 partition. Not without additional software, even then I don't know of anything off hand that would allow it.

So Linux is safe. Worst that windows could do would be to overwrite or delete the partition, but that is unlikely to happen by accident.

There are two things,

1) Windows would need ext drivers to read the contents.

2) Windows would still have the ability to modify the partitions and could wipe the partition clean.

So, could it be a problem? Yes. Is it likely to happen? No.

Depending on what work you are doing, I would rather install VirtualBox and then run a Windows VM to do your work.

If you can, I would suggest two separate disks. I've seen an MBR update (Windows side) fuck with the GRUB boot (Linux side) on the same disk. I never seem to have issues when I had the two on separated. Don't dual boot Windows anymore so my info may be dated.
